speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development (a) how many Day Activity Centres (DACs) are there currently; (b) how many young adults aged 18-21 are enrolled in the DACs currently; and (c) how many special needs trained educators or caregivers are there in the DACs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: DACs equip PWDs with skills to enable them to live as independently as possible at home and within the community.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Clients attending DACs are supported by a care team comprising professionals and direct care workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The professional staff includes psychologists, therapists and social workers, and they formulate the care plans as well as supervise and conduct activities, such as behavioural modifications, therapy and counselling.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Apart from being equipped with professional training and direct care knowledge, the staff working in DACs also attend courses to improve their skills in communicating with PWDs and understanding their needs.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I understand that a number of caregivers had previously experienced some form of challenges and difficulty in enrolling their children who are aged 18 and above into DACs after they have graduated from special education (SPED) schools.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: So, my question to the Minister of State is whether there are enough places to meet the demand and whether there are enough DAC professionals to attend to these young adults in the DACs.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: And what is the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) doing to ensure that parents and guardians are aware of the various options available for young adults aged 18 and above after they graduate from SPED schools.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: My second supplementary question is whether there are plans to consolidate all the DACs into specialised centres for further training for such young adults to better prepare them to be work-ready, and if there are plans to ensure that there are targeted SkillsFuture certification programmes for them so that, ultimately, they can be independent.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: I shall try to answer the last question first.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: All these VWOs have their own background, culture, strengths, expertise and capabilities.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: So, I think it is not so feasible nor practical to try to artificially consolidate them just to make sure that they are able to deliver quality programmes and services.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: What MSF does is that we issue guidelines and standards to all the DACs to ensure that they will follow a certain regime and protocol when they roll out the programmes and services to their clients.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: MSF also conducts periodical onsite audits to check on DACs to ensure that standards are met.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: For some of the DACs which fail to meet the standards, MSF officers will work together with the DAC management to identify the gaps to develop the service improvement programmes so as to make sure that they are able to meet the requirements and better serve their clients.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: As to SkillsFuture training, this is, indeed, something that we are looking at.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: We will conduct these training when the feasibility studies are concluded to make sure that the clients at the DACs will be given the opportunity for lifelong learning under the SkillsFuture Framework.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: For those who need to work, such SkillsFuture-certified courses will enhance their employment prospects.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: Once ready, that will be another step to give a leg-up to the clients at the DACs.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: As to the Member's first supplementary question of post-18 transition, we are aware of the challenges faced by PWDs and also their caregivers.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: We have also been discussing and organising with the DACs to stage exhibitions, talks and sharing experiences by caregivers at the SPED schools and also to conduct orientation programmes for their caregivers before the age of 18.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: We are also working closely with MOE on this aspect.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: The purpose is to make sure that before they reach the age of 18, the caregivers are given the understanding and also to be better prepared for them to make a decision, post 18, which DAC to go to and so on and so forth.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: There was another part of the Member's supplementary question, the different options.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: If I may invite the Member to elaborate on this.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: The options among the different DACs if they wish to specialise in specific areas.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: It ties in with my other question on SkillsFuture certification.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: Different DACs offer different types of services and programmes so that they are able to offer a myriad of courses and training to meet the different and diverse needs of PWDs.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: There are quite a lot of options available.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: As mentioned just now, the important thing is to provide adequate information to PWDs and their caregivers so that they understand the range of services and programmes offered by the different DACs so that they will be able to make an informed choice of which DAC to go to when they reach the age of 18.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: This solution would not be easy and will be quite costly.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: And we need to get rid of some boxes of thinking to come to a better solution, because the needs are going to increase, going to be more costly, and there is no way that anyone, VWO, any kind person or organisation that can do it on their own.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: So, I would like to ask the Ministry to consider setting up a small task force just to specifically look at this very challenging area of the special needs community.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: I want to thank the Member for that very passionate plea.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: We also share the same commitment in wanting to uplift PWDs in our community.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: The Member has hit the nail on the head.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: To enable, to uplift this segment of our population, it needs to go beyond the DACs, it needs to go beyond the Government.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: It really needs the community to come together, working together with the DACs and with the Government to ensure that we would be able to provide adequate support, not just to PWDs but also the DACs running the services and programmes for them.
